question: Articles 34, 35, 37 and 42 of the Digital Services Act (DSA)1 establish risk assessment, mitigation, auditing and reporting obligations. In cases where the same AI model supports both a designated search service and non-designated conversational functionalities, mitigation measures may affect users beyond the designated service. 1.

Should providers document whether measures adopted to mitigate risks under Article 35 also alter the outputs or functioning of non-designated AI functionalities, including private conversations? If not, how are such collateral effects assessed?

Will the Commission require or examine evidence that compares model behaviour before and after any significant DSA-related mitigation measures are enforced, including unintended restrictions on lawful expression, information quality or viewpoint diversity?

Which existing DSA reporting or auditing requirements would make the nature, justification and fundamental-rights impact of such changes publicly verifiable and what information would remain confidential?

Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 19 October 2022 on a single market For Digital Services and amending Directive 2000/31/EC (Digital Services Act), OJ L 277, 27.10.2022, p. 1, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2022/2065/oj.
